title: A community pH index of English river invertebrates did not follow site pH change from 2000-2007 to 2016-2025 at 1,144 sites; soft northern streams gained acid-sensitive Heptageniidae
abstract: We tested whether river invertebrates at English Environment Agency (EA) sites followed pH recovery from acid deposition as far as the spatial pH-composition relation predicts. This is an independent test of a Swedish lake result (tracking ratio 0.66-0.85). We joined EA kick samples (spring and autumn, 1995-2025, family level) with pH from the EA Water Quality API at points within 500 m (1,144 sites). A community pH index used cross-fitted family pH optima. The spatial slope was clear (0.065 index units per pH unit), but index change did not follow pH change: the tracking ratio was -0.04 (95% interval -0.12 to 0.04). Presence weights, sample thinning, a pollution-score covariate, network-change adjustment, annual panels with lags, and windows after a probable 2005-2007 laboratory step in the pH record gave -0.17 to 0.05. At 20 soft northern sites, pH increased by 0.41, and the index predicts +0.027; the observed change was -0.003 (-0.010 to 0.005). Post hoc, an index with river type removed gave 0.05 (soft sites 0.21, -0.07 to 0.50), and an index trained only on soft sites gave 0.11 (-0.02 to 0.26). The English pH gradient mainly separates lowland from upland rivers, so a network-wide index is not a valid recovery target. Exploratory: acid-sensitive Heptageniidae occurrence increased by 0.24 at soft northern sites and not at soft south-western sites, where pH did not change; Baetidae and Ephemerellidae did not show this. Wet winters and the 2018 and 2022 droughts did not set back soft sites; summer rain and warmth had small negative autumn slopes. Limitations: only 5 sites below pH 6.5, a probable laboratory step in pH, family level only, and a post hoc taxon result. Source data stay external (OGL); code, site-level derived tables, aggregate results and figures are included.
